topic: Process Technology Development and Scale-up Gaps, from Conceptual Design to Commercial Deployment
title: Process Technology Development and Scale-up Gaps, from Conceptual Design to Commercial Deployment
session_title: Concept to Commercialization: Considerations for Process Design and Scale Up - Session 2 (Invited Talks)
abstract: This presentation will examine gaps in process technology development and scaleup timeline, from conceptual design to commercial deployment. We will explore how these gaps arise when technology changes hands, either between direct actors (academia, government, small & large businesses), change of main source of funding (government, philanthropy, industry, investors, lenders), and dominant risk profile (R&D, tech scaling, commercialization.) Furthermore, we will propose that increasing collaborative approaches throughout the technology lifetime lessen these negative effects by incorporating different, often complementary as well as sometimes confronted, insights from different stakeholder groups reflecting their intrinsic priorities and biases.
presenting_author: Ignasi Palou Rivera | Refinity, Orlando, FL
authors: Ignasi Palou Rivera | Refinity, Orlando, FL

topic: From Biomass to Biochemicals in Research and Startup Companies
title: From Biomass to Biochemicals in Research and Startup Companies
session_title: Concept to Commercialization: Considerations for Process Design and Scale Up - Session 2 (Invited Talks)
abstract: Renewable cellulose and lignin are abundant and available as the sustainable feedstock of the future for next generation chemicals and materials. In the Dauenhauer laboratory, research has focused on the relationships between catalyst design and development, process design and optimization, and laboratory-to-market strategy to create new markets for biochemicals and biomaterials. Three parallel examples outline the utilization of lignocellulosic biomass to create economic value in the fields of surfactants, acrylics and acrylates, and general carbon products such as carbon co-feeds or carbon credits. Examples are presented in the context of general strategy to pursue business opportunities competitive with conventional processes based on fossil fuels including identification of potential new chemical businesses, evaluation of biomass supply potential, and optimization of the expansive number of parameters required to create a successful commercial chemical and materials business.
presenting_author: Paul Dauenhauer | University of Minnesota, Shoreview, MN
authors: Paul Dauenhauer | University of Minnesota, Shoreview, MN
